clearedSpotChecks.check: Can an ordinary account link a HyperCore spot token to the PoolManager address, so that HyperCore credits or debits through it?
clearedSpotChecks.note: I fetched the transfers page again on 2026-11-27. Line 60 says that for a contract deployed by a contract, the first storage slot or the slot at keccak256("HyperCore deployer") must hold the finalizer, and line 62 says the finalizer must match the value in that slot. On https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm at block 0x31fcb3f, slot 0 of 0x12D4Fd9C5DeDd00ab8a0bCe2CF0167bbf94b6B1F holds 0x2d09d0c2f82c59b19b3c65a48ce2c550bf0921f9, the owner. That fits lib/solmate/src/auth/Owned.sol:17, the first base in the linearisation of src/PoolManager.sol:80 through src/ProtocolFees.sol:15. The custom slot 0x8c306a6a12fff1951878e8621be6674add1102cd359dd968efbbe797629ef84f reads zero. I computed it with the repository's keccak in tools/opdiff/evm.py:64 and checked that keccak against the hash of the empty input. The only raw-slot SSTOREs in src/ are src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:73 and src/libraries/Pool.sol:547. Both write to mapping-derived slots, so a caller cannot make either of them hit that slot without a keccak preimage. If the deployer was an EOA, the create-nonce finalizer is the deployer itself, which is a privileged party. The clearance holds.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Standard battery (99,985 vectors) and targeted set (85,544 vectors) rerun on the official node at head about 52,411,100 (2026-11-27), covering MULMOD, ADDMOD, the 512 bit mulDiv shape, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, SIGNEXTEND, SAR, SHL, SHR, BYTE, EXP, the comparisons, JUMPI, KECCAK256, MCOPY and CALLDATALOAD.
clearedSpotChecks.note: battery-official.log ends with 'ran 99985/99985 mismatches 0 errors 0' and gives per-opcode counts, including 8,359 MULDIV512, 8,359 MULMOD and 7,921 each for SAR, SHL, SHR, BYTE and SIGNEXTEND. targeted-official.log ends with 'ran 85544/85544 mismatches 0 errors 0', including 21,074 MULDIV512 and 24,154 MULMOD. I did not rerun them. Both logs support the stated result. One limit carries over from cycle 24: eth_call shows the RPC node's execution path, and whether the closed hl-node producer runs the same path cannot be seen from outside. The mined swap checks and the replica receipts-root equality cover part of that gap.

clearedSpotChecks.note: I ran eth_getCode myself on 2026-11-27. CoreWriter 0x3333...3333 returns 544 bytes with sha256 fd053fae...dac83, and 0x2222...2222 returns 122 bytes with sha256 89c9f51d...816a. Both are equal to precomp36.json. eth_call with a 32 byte zero input returns 0x at 0x0815, so the address is empty, and returns data at 0x0814, so the precompile answers. Both results match the stated range. I also read the PoolManager's code: 24,009 bytes with sha256 prefix 907b85e610ad5dab, equal to networks.json.
